industries.rationale: The bill explicitly targets patent expediting for AI, semiconductor design, and quantum computing, all core technology-sector activities.

bill.plainSummary: This bill directs the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office to create a pilot program that speeds up patent reviews for inventions in critical and emerging technology areas, specifically artificial intelligence, semiconductor design, and quantum information science. The office would be required to report to Congress on how well the program works. The goal is to reduce waiting times for patents in these strategic technology fields.

bill.title: Rural Development Hospital Technical Assistance Program Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry.

industries.rationale: The bill directly targets rural hospitals, providing them with technical assistance, training, and support for operational and financial improvements.
The program explicitly includes increasing telehealth capabilities as a development need, which would affect broadband and telecommunications infrastructure providers serving rural hospitals.
The bill addresses acquiring and upgrading health care information systems including electronic health records, which would involve technology vendors and IT service providers.
The program covers technical assistance for constructing, expanding, and modernizing health care facilities, which would involve construction and engineering firms.

bill.plainSummary: This bill formally establishes a technical assistance program within the Department of Agriculture to help rural hospitals (in areas with 50,000 or fewer residents) improve their operations and finances. The program would provide training and support to help these hospitals modernize facilities, expand telehealth, upgrade information systems, and navigate USDA loan and grant programs. Priority would go to hospitals already participating in certain USDA rural assistance programs, and USDA would report annually to Congress on the program's results.

plain.whoItTouches: Farmers, and anyone who buys food.

bill.title: Whole Milk for Healthy Kids Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Became Public Law No: 119-69.

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects dairy producers and processors by expanding the types of milk schools may purchase and serve.
Schools participating in the lunch program face new training requirements and changes to meal planning and procurement rules.
Food service companies and suppliers to school meal programs would adjust product offerings to meet the expanded milk and nondairy beverage options.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would allow schools participating in the National School Lunch Program to offer whole milk and 2% milk to students, in addition to the low-fat and fat-free options currently required. It would expand nondairy milk alternatives, permit parents (not just doctors) to request milk substitutes for students with dietary restrictions, and exclude milk fat from saturated fat limits in school meals. The bill also requires annual food allergy training and certification for school food service staff.

bill.title: A joint resolution terminating the national emergency declared to impose global tariffs.
bill.latestActionText: Held at the desk.
subjects: Presidents and presidential powers, Vice Presidents

industries.rationale: Manufacturers that import components or materials would see input costs change if the tariffs are removed.
Retailers and consumer goods companies that import finished products would face different cost structures depending on whether the tariffs remain.
Agricultural exporters and importers are directly affected by tariff policy and potential retaliatory measures from trading partners.
Technology companies that import hardware, semiconductors, or components face cost changes tied to tariff levels.
Shipping, logistics, and freight companies handle import volumes that shift with tariff policy changes.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would end the national emergency that President Trump declared on April 2, 2025, which authorized a 10% tariff on most goods imported into the United States and higher tariffs on certain trading partners. Terminating the emergency would remove the legal basis for those tariffs. The resolution is a legislative tool for Congress to check executive emergency powers related to trade policy.

bill.title: Holocaust Expropriated Art Recovery Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Became Public Law No: 119-82.
subjects: War crimes, genocide, crimes against humanity

industries.rationale: The bill creates new procedural pathways and limits defenses in civil litigation, expanding the scope and duration of claims that law firms may pursue or defend.
Museums and cultural institutions that hold or exhibit artwork are directly affected by expanded liability and procedural rules for restitution claims.
Banks and auction houses that handle art transactions or hold art as collateral face potential claims if works in their possession are subject to restitution.

bill.plainSummary: This bill removes the 2026 deadline for filing lawsuits to recover art and other property taken during Nazi persecution between 1933 and 1945. It makes it easier to sue foreign governments and defendants located anywhere in the United States, and it blocks certain legal defenses that courts have used to dismiss these claims, such as arguments that too much time has passed. The changes apply to cases already filed as well as future ones.

bill.title: A joint resolution proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States relating to the authority of Congress and the States to regulate contributions and expenditures intended to affect elections and to enact public financing systems for political campaigns.
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: The amendment would reshape campaign finance law, directly affecting lobbying firms and attorneys who advise on election spending and compliance.
Advocacy organizations that spend money to influence elections would face new regulatory authority over their fundraising and expenditures.
Regulations on election spending could affect advertising revenue and the market for political communications services.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution proposes a constitutional amendment that would allow Congress and state governments to set limits on how much money candidates and others can raise and spend to influence elections. It would also permit them to create public financing systems for campaigns and to treat corporations differently from individual people, including by prohibiting corporations from spending money on elections. The amendment would require ratification by three-fourths of the states to take effect.

bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance. (Sponsor introductory remarks on measure: CR S7964)

industries.rationale: The bill creates a new Medicare payment stream for ground ambulance services that do not result in transport, directly affecting ambulance operators' revenues and service models.
Medicare payment policy changes for emergency medical services affect the program's costs and may influence private insurers' coverage decisions for similar services.

Payment rates would generally match what Medicare currently pays when a patient is transported. The Government Accountability Office would study how the program affects Medicare beneficiaries' access to emergency medical services and their health outcomes.

bill.title: Patients Deserve Price Tags Act
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 522.
subjects: Department of Health and Human Services
Drug safety, medical device, and laboratory regulation

industries.rationale: The bill directly imposes new price-disclosure obligations on hospitals and surgical centers, changing their administrative and compliance requirements.
Medical device costs must be included in the price estimates, affecting how device manufacturers' products are priced and disclosed to patients.
Price transparency requirements may affect how insurers negotiate rates and how patients understand their coverage and out-of-pocket costs.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would require hospitals, ambulatory surgical centers, and other healthcare facilities to provide patients with upfront price estimates for scheduled procedures and services. The estimates would need to include costs for the facility, physicians, anesthesia, medical devices, and other associated charges. Facilities that fail to provide these price disclosures could face civil penalties.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
